claims.reason: `hcomm` is an argument only because of `include hcomm hpb in`. No other binder mentions it (the type of `hpb` mentions only p', p'', q', q''), and neither does the conclusion, so the statement still elaborates without it. It is still provable: apply hpb to (0, 0). The condition q' 0 = q'' 0 holds since both are 0 by map_zero. This gives a unique b with p' b = 0 and p'' b = 0. Both 0 (map_zero) and b₁ - b₂ (map_sub with h', h'') satisfy these equations, so uniqueness gives b₁ - b₂ = 0, and sub_eq_zero gives b₁ = b₂. All maps are ring homs, so there is no gap and no degenerate case (if B is trivial the conclusion holds outright). The original proof used hcomm only to supply the condition at (p' b₁, p'' b₁), which the pair (0, 0) makes unnecessary.
